Ben Horowitz on Databricks CEO Ali Ghodsi: "You just don't get this good of a market opportunity with this good of an entrepreneur. That's the rarest of rare things."

Despite surpassing a $7 billion run rate and growing 80% year over year, Databricks might be the most under the radar story in Silicon Valley.

Three years ago, every interaction on Databricks involved a human. Today, the company is seeing more queries from agents than people.

Ali believes AGI is already here. Yet inside most companies today, AI still isn't trusted to reliably update records in Salesforce.

"AI does not have an intelligence problem," Ali explains. "It has a context problem."

Even the smartest human would be all but useless without access to the company's data, permission to act, feedback, or the knowledge in other employees' heads. Ali's answer is what he calls a "system of record for agents."

But the bigger question is how agents will change the firm itself.

85 years ago, James Burnham's The Managerial Revolution described how a small class of professional managers centralized the decision-making inside of companies. Today, thanks to a new wave of technology, the craft practitioners at the front lines are regaining responsibility again. The irony is that the decline of managerialism may look more like everyone becoming a manager.

In this issue of Profiles of the Future, @bhorowitz and @mikemcg0 explain how seven Berkeley academics built Databricks, and why it will power the future of the firm: https://www.a16z.news/p/databricks-and-the-future-of-the

They explore why high standards make kids happier, how HAA is using motivation and real-world building to redesign college, what parents need to believe before choosing a new kind of school, why Joe expects AI to drive an explosion in entrepreneurship, and why Gagan thinks students should pick what they care about over whichever field seems safest from AI.

About a decade ago, Databricks got an acquisition offer at roughly six times its valuation at the time. CEO Ali Ghodsi tells the story of the conversation with Ben Horowitz that made him turn it down:

Ben: "You just don't get this good of a market opportunity with this good of an entrepreneur. That's the rarest of rare things."

"We see great entrepreneurs, but their market opportunity is limited, and then we see companies that have a great market opportunity, but the entrepreneur is not big enough to fulfill that... But this was a case where we had both."

Ali: "The acquisition offer was on the table... I had made the mistake of telling my co-founders, and they were like, 'Take your hands off the keyboard. Nobody work anymore. We're done here. Let's count my money.'"

"And I was like, 'Maybe they're right. Maybe we should just sell.' And I remember having that conversation with Ben."

"He said, 'If you sell for this number, it's really great for me. I'll pay the investors back many times over... But if you're like me, you're gonna look back the rest of your life thinking, I missed that one shot. I should have taken it all the way. And now I'll never know how far I could have taken it. So do you wanna live with that, or do you wanna just have the money?'"

"And I was like, 'Okay, thanks.' Hung up the phone. 'We're never doing this. This is not happening.'"

很多时候读AI生成的回答，哪怕内容完全正确，读上几段就会觉得异常疲惫、喘不过气。

来自纽约大学和德克萨斯大学奥斯汀分校的语言学研究人员，通过对 14 个主流大模型与人类真实文本的横向对比，揭示了这种“心累感”背后的真正元凶：

前沿AI模型正在系统性地过度使用 6 类极其消耗人类工作记忆的语言结构...

为什么 AI 写出来的东西读着这么累？

人类日常交流遵循一条内在铁律：在“表达省力”和“理解省力”之间寻找平衡。但当下的前沿模型却彻底倒向了极限压缩与高密度，制造了六大阅读路障：

生造生僻短语（冷门搭配）模型喜欢把两个罕见的词硬拼在一起，比如造出“读者耐心预算（reader-patience budget）”这类人类几乎不用的怪异词组，迫使大脑在理解时卡顿半秒。

长距离语法割裂（主谓严重脱节）模型习惯在主语和核心谓语之间塞入冗长修饰语，例如“一只总是能站起来并跑掉的猫，是一只更冷静的猫”。主语和结论被拉得极远，读到后半句时，人脑前面积攒的工作记忆已经被耗空。

强行删掉连接词（省略连接代词）为了追求字数上的精简，模型常把“the book that the professor wrote”中的 that 直接抹掉，变成“the book the professor wrote”。表面上省了一个词，实际却模糊了从句边界，增加了快速扫读时的误读率。

名词像糖葫芦一样死板堆叠诸如“恐怖电影原声带生成器（horror movie soundtrack generator）”这类名词串，完全省去了逻辑介词，迫使读者自己去逆向拆解“到底谁在修饰谁”。

不合习惯的名词动用把不该作动词的名词硬搬成动词，比如把“记在日历里”直接缩写成“calendar it”。机器觉得紧凑，人读起来却极度别扭。

对没有生命的物体强行拟人化比如写出“整场对话正在咬自己的尾巴（eating its own tail）”。虽然隐喻意图可以被猜出来，但抽象事物搭配强动作性动词，会给读者的具象思维带来额外的认知摩擦。

OpenAI disclosed an unauthenticated remote code execution bug in Brotli, the compression library inside Node.js, Bun and Envoy, found by its own agents during red-teaming. An unpatched server that accepts compressed input can be taken over by a malicious client, with no account needed. The root cause was fixed in the source in February, but nobody knew it was a security hole, so no release shipped.

The same month, OpenAI finished two months leading a coalition to patch php2shell. levelsio's advice to anyone running a VPS passed 10,000 bookmarks: get it off the public internet.

the default that costs you: SSH and web ports open to the whole internet, guarded by a good key. A key stops password guessing. It does nothing against an exploit in the software listening on the port.

what to do this week, in this order:

1. Run tailscale up on the server and your laptop, then SSH in over the Tailscale IP.
2. Only once that works: ufw default deny incoming, then ufw allow in on tailscale0 to any port 22.
3. Put the site behind Cloudflare Tunnel, or allow 443 only from Cloudflare's IP ranges.
4. Update Node.js and anything else that bundles Brotli.

the check: from a network outside your tailnet, nc -zv your-server-ip 22 should time out.

After the ports, I run a full audit checklist over the site itself, since the open port was only the first door.

Tailscale and Cloudflare Tunnel are both free at this scale.

the security audit prompt I run once the ports are locked:

https://godofprompt.ai/prompt-library/create-website-security-checklist
follow if you ship on your own servers. I post the fixes the week the bugs land.

Someone plugged Claude Code into his cheap car stereo and found a root backdoor, a hidden call recorder and a mic that never turned off.

If you own a cheap Android TV box, tablet or car stereo, yours could be doing the same.

Here are 6 prompts to run the same audit ↓

Prompt 6: Permission audit (Android phone)

"List every app with mic, camera, location or contacts permission and when it last used each. Flag background mic or location use. Suggest what to revoke, wait for my OK."

iPhone: Settings → Privacy & Security → App Privacy Report.

Rules: only devices you own, back up first, make it ask before every change.

More free Claude prompts, no signup:
